reader.requirement: At --std 85 an out-of-line format 4 PERFORM must accept at least six AFTER phrases (identifiers or index-names, TEST BEFORE or TEST AFTER) and execute them by the 1985 general rules; more than six is implementor latitude, and the in-line form, which SR2 forbids an AFTER phrase, is not a host for them.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.PerformVaryingInitInnerBeforeAugmentOuter (from 2002): at 85 the outer variable is augmented before the inner one is set (§1985:VI.6.21.4 GR10), from 2002 the inner one is set first
inline-perform-after-2002 refuses an AFTER phrase under an inline PERFORM below 2002 (COBOL0900); perform-varying-by-omitted-2002 refuses an omitted BY

reader.edition-search: Read BindVarying (the AFTER list is an unbounded performVaryingAfter* loop with no count limit at any edition) and the VersionConformancePass PERFORM visitors; grep of DialectBehavior in the PERFORM binder.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: with an AFTER FROM that depends on an outer variable the 1985 arm augments the outer item first (pf6a2 at 85: 3 executions, 3333333) while 2023 sets the inner item first (pf6a at 2023: 29 executions, 3222222); the number of AFTER phrases admitted is the same
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness writes exactly six AFTER phrases over identifiers with literal FROM values under TEST BEFORE; it does not exercise more than six, index-names, TEST AFTER, an AFTER FROM that depends on an outer variable (the 1985 ordering), or the in-line refusal

probes.expected: six AFTERs each FROM the next-outer item: by §1985:VI.6.21.4 GR10 (outer augmented, inner set to the new FROM, an AFTER item re-cycled only when its preceding item is augmented) 3 executions ending all 3; seven AFTERs with TEST AFTER and two index-names: 2^8 = 256

probes.printed: COBOL0900: an AFTER phrase in an inline PERFORM requires COBOL-2002 (targeting COBOL-85)
probes.expected: §1985:VI.6.21.3 SR2: in format 4 with procedure-name-1 omitted, AFTER must not be specified

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.6.21.3 SR12  (6.21.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR12
OK  §1985:VI.6.21.3 SR2  (6.21.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2

reader.notes: The grammar's performVaryingAfter* and BindVarying's level list have no upper bound, so six, seven or more AFTER phrases bind and run; the 1985 execution order comes from the PerformVaryingInitInnerBeforeAugmentOuter dialect behavior being off at 85. The expected 3 for the dependent-FROM case was traced by hand from the GR10 text and the closing sentence that an AFTER item cycles each time the preceding item is augmented; the GR10 ordering itself belongs to the GR rows (kb/Work PB5101 per the code comment).

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VI.6.21.3 SR2, SR7, SR8, SR12 and VI.6.21.4 GR10d. pa1.cob at --std 85: out-of-line VARYING plus six AFTER phrases mixing an index-name varied FROM an index-name (X2 FROM X0), a negative BY identifier (BY M1 = -1), an index-name FROM a literal, and an AFTER whose FROM and UNTIL depend on the outermost item (I6 FROM I1 UNTIL I6 > I1 + 1): N=130, which is the 1985 trace (64 for I1=1; for I1=2 the first I6 cycle starts at the value set while I1 was 1, giving 3+15*2 I6 values times 2 = 66); --std 2023 also 130, as expected since the dependent FROM is not on the immediately outer item. Index-name inside an arithmetic expression refused COBOL1637 (outside this rule). cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.21.3 SR12; OK §1985:VI.6.21.4 GR10d.
